pool.text: Two drama schools, the French-speaking Conservatoire Royal and the Koninklijk Conservatorium, were founded.
The Cantillon Brewery, a lambic brewery, was founded in the city.
Pralines were first introduced by Jean Neuhaus II in the Royal Saint-Hubert Galleries.
The Centenary Palace was built for the World Fair on the Heysel Plateau.
The British Guards Armoured Division liberated the city.
The Treaty of Brussels was signed as a prelude to an alliance.
The North-South connection linking main railway stations was completed.
The Atomium modernist structure was built for the World Fair.
Underground lines known as the premetro have been serviced by tramways since this year.
The first premetro underground tram service was launched.
The first Metro line was opened in the city.
The Brussels Metro dates back to this specific year in history.
The officially bilingual Brussels-Capital Region was created.
The city was named European Capital of Culture.
The winter activities known as Winter Wonders were launched.
Brussels has had a car-sharing service operated by the Bremen company Cambio.
A public bicycle-sharing programme was introduced in the city during this year.
STIB/MIVB has been operating a night bus network called Noctis since April.
The night-time public transport service has been supplemented by Collecto, a shared taxi system.
The Zen Car electric car-sharing scheme was launched in the university and European areas.
